item.title: North Korea Human Rights Hearing Held in U.S. Congress: "Must Be a Core Agenda in Any Negotiations" (美의회서 북한 인권 청문회 열려… “어떤 협상서도 핵심 의제 돼야”)
item.description:
The Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, a bipartisan human rights body within the U.S. Congress, held a hearing on North Korean human rights on the 28th for the first time in several years. At this hearing, themed "North Korean Human Rights Activism: Current Prospects and Obstacles," Chairman and Republican House Representative Chris Smith pointed out that North Korea is "one of the most repressive regimes in the world," operating an "unimaginably horrific system of oppression for decades," enforced through widespread torture, deprivation of freedom of expression, religion, and movement, extensive digital and social surveillance, arbitrary detention, and a vast system of forced labor camps. (미 의회 내 초당적 인권 기구인 ‘톰 랜토스 인권위원회가’ 28일 몇 년 만에 북한 인권 청문회를 열었다. ‘북한 인권 운동: 현재의 전망과 장애물’이란 주제로 열린 이번 청문회에서 위원장인 크리스 스미스 공화당 하원의원은 북한이 “세계에서 가장 억압적인 정권 가운데 하나”라며 “수십 년째 상상하기 힘든 끔찍한 억압 체계를 운영하고 있으며 광범위한 고문과 표현·종교·이동의 자유 박탈, 광범위한 디지털·사회적 감시와 임의 구금, 방대한 강제 노동 수용소 체계 등을 통해 이를 강제하고 있다”고 지적했다.)

Smith emphasized the importance of information flow into North Korea, stating, "Information is a force for change, and any attempt to block it, wherever it occurs, must be taken as seriously as possible," adding that "every effort by the regime to prevent (information inflow) only makes that information more precious and powerful." Susan Scholte, chair of the North Korea Freedom Coalition, who appeared as a witness, read a testimony from Kim Ji-young, CEO of Free North Korea Radio, who first secretly listened to foreign radio broadcasts at age 13, stating, "The most powerful force to change North Korea is not military power but information," and "Information changes people, and changed people eventually change society." (스미스는 대북 정보 유입의 중요성을 강조하며 “정보는 변화를 이끄는 힘이고, 정보를 차단하려는 시도는 어디서 일어나든 최대한 심각하게 받아들여야 한다”며 “정권이 (정보 유입을) 막으려는 모든 노력이 오히려 그 정보를 더욱 소중하고 강력하게 만든다”고 했다. 증인으로 출석한 수잰 숄티 북한자유연합 의장은 13세 때 처음 외부 라디오 방송을 몰래 들었다는 김지영 자유북한라디오 대표의 증언을 대독하며 “북한을 바꿀 수 있는 가장 강력한 힘은 군사력이 아닌 정보” “정보가 사람을 바꾸고 바뀐 사람이 결국 사회를 바꾼다”고 했다.)

Scholte noted that "this is the most challenging period in the history of North Korean human rights activism," as Radio Free Asia (RFA) and Voice of America (VOA), which played crucial roles in publicizing human rights conditions in North Korea and facilitating information inflow, are struggling to function amid the restructuring under the second Trump administration. In South Korea, under the administration of President Lee Jae-myung’s policy of dialogue with the North, the survival of various North Korean human rights groups has become uncertain. Smith criticized measures such as South Korea's suspension of broadcasts into North Korea, the abolition of the human rights office under the Ministry of Unification, and legislative support for banning anti-North Korea leaflets, calling them "actions that directly affect civil society, especially groups led by North Korean defectors, which carry out one of the most effective means of communication with North Korean residents—information delivery." (숄티는 “지금이 북한 인권 운동 역사상 가장 도전적인 시기”라고 했는데, 북한 내 인권 상황 공론화와 대북 정보 유입에 결정적인 역할을 했던 자유아시아방송(RFA)·미국의소리(VOA) 등은 트럼프 2기 정부의 구조조정 여파로 제 기능을 하지 못하고 있다. 한국 역시 이재명 정부의 대북 대화 기조 속 여러 대북 인권 단체들의 생존이 불투명한 상황이 됐다. 스미스는 한국 정부의 대북 방송 중단, 통일부의 인권 업무 사무소 폐지, 대북 전단 금지 입법 지원 등을 거론하며 “북한 주민들과의 가장 효과적인 소통 방식 가운데 하나인 정보 전달을 수행하는 시민사회, 특히 탈북민 주도 단체에 직접적으로 영향을 미치는 조치들”이라 비판했다.)

In a VOA interview after the hearing, Smith mentioned that human rights issues were not properly addressed in past nuclear negotiations, asserting that human rights must be "an absolutely core agenda in any situation." He also stated that the hearing would serve as a catalyst to review follow-up measures, including additional legislation. Meanwhile, Scholte, regarding the forced repatriation of North Korean defectors, accused China of clearly violating the UN Refugee Convention it signed, urging that "defectors forcibly repatriated face torture, imprisonment, or even execution upon returning to North Korea" and that "sanctions under the Magnitsky Act should be imposed." (스미스는 청문회 이후 가진 VOA 인터뷰에서는 과거 핵 협상에서 북한 인권 문제가 제대로 다뤄지지 않은 점을 언급하며 어떤 상황에서도 인권이 “절대적으로 핵심 의제가 돼야 한다”고 했다. 이번 청문회를 계기로 추가 입법을 포함한 후속 조치도 검토하겠다고 밝혔다. 한편 숄티는 탈북민 강제 북송(北送) 문제와 관련해 중국이 자신이 서명한 유엔난민협약을 명백하게 위반하고 있다며 “강제 송환된 탈북민들은 북한으로 돌아가면 고문, 투옥, 심지어 처형이 기다린다” “마그니츠키법에 따른 제재를 부과해야 한다”고 촉구했다.)

item.title: New Equipment Received, Old Equipment Sold Used… Workplace Disaster Prevention Funds Gone to Waste (새 설비 받고 헌 설비는 중고 매각… 눈먼 돈 된 산재 예방 지원금)
item.description:
The government spent 654 billion won to support private companies with new equipment, urging them to replace old machinery to prevent industrial accidents. However, it was revealed that 77% of the recipient companies kept the new equipment while either continuing to use the old machinery or selling it to other businesses. Additionally, 60% of smart safety equipment, funded with 81.7 billion won by the government, was not being used properly. <<> On the 29th, the Government Joint Anti-Corruption Promotion Team under the Office for Government Policy Coordination, along with the Ministry of Employment and Labor, announced that these issues were identified during an inspection of industrial accident prevention projects carried out by the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA). <<> These industrial accident prevention projects are funded by the Industrial Accident Insurance Fund, which is financed by premiums paid by business owners. KOSHA supports private workplaces with smart safety equipment, aids in replacing hazardous or old machinery, and provides safety consulting. Annual expenditures average over 1 trillion won, with last year's budget reaching 1.2931 trillion won. <<> Among these, for the old and hazardous equipment replacement project, which has received 654 billion won since 2024, only 933 out of 4,111 workplaces (22.7%) that received new equipment in 2024 actually disposed of their old machinery. The remaining 3,178 workplaces (77.3%) either continued using old equipment without safety measures, moved it to other sites for continued use, or sold it to other companies, rendering the project ineffective in stopping the use of old, hazardous machinery. Several workplaces also received more equipment than they originally had, resulting in expansion rather than replacement. <<> In the smart safety equipment support project, which has received 81.7 billion won since 2023, it was found that 207 out of 345 supported devices (60%) were either left unused or operated with safety features turned off. Specifically, 80% of vehicle collision prevention devices, 76% of muscle-assist suits, 64% of smart electric forklifts, and 50% of AI-based human detection systems were being misused. <<> Some companies even defrauded the smart safety equipment support program. Company A conspired with an industrial cleaning robot seller, purchasing robots at inflated prices. They submitted forged tax invoices to KOSHA to receive reimbursement for the robots. The seller then returned part of the difference between the inflated and actual price in cash. Company B similarly colluded with a human detection system seller, buying systems at inflated prices. They submitted inflated cost statements for materials and labor related to manufacturing and installation to KOSHA, receiving system payments, and also received cash kickbacks from the seller. <<> The promotion team confirmed that 189 additional companies purchased the same type of equipment as Companies A and B and received subsidies. It has requested an investigation from law enforcement authorities. The team announced that Companies A and B, along with others, fraudulently received 81 subsidies totaling 1.86 billion won, and plans to recover 9.4 billion won, including penalty surcharges. <<> In the support project for safety facility costs at small construction sites, it was found that 571 cases totaling 3.5 billion won were provided to ineligible sites. Companies manipulated contract amounts or split a single project into multiple parts to appear as small-scale construction sites to obtain subsidies. There were also 29 cases of receiving duplicate subsidies from multiple government agencies. <<> The government stated it would improve the system to prevent fund leakage. The old and hazardous equipment replacement support project will verify whether old equipment is disposed of, and the safety equipment support project will set upper limits per item. For construction site support, follow-up management procedures, including reviewing construction contracts, will be strengthened. <<> Kim Young-soo, Deputy Minister of the Office for Government Policy Coordination and head of the promotion team, said, “The government is swiftly pursuing follow-up measures based on these inspection results and will periodically monitor implementation to prevent recurrence of illegal or inappropriate cases.” He added, “We plan to operate these industrial accident prevention projects more efficiently to eliminate hazardous and risk factors at industrial sites and thoroughly protect workers’ lives and safety.” (정부가 산업재해 예방을 위해 낡은 설비를 교체하라며 6540억원을 들여 민간 기업들에 신규 설비를 지원했으나, 지원받은 기업 77%가 신규 설비를 챙겨놓고 낡은 설비도 그대로 쓰거나 다른 기업에 팔아치운 것으로 드러났다. 정부가 817억원을 들여 지원한 스마트 안전 장비는 60%가 제대로 쓰이지 않고 있었다.)
